rationale: No displayed candidate plausibly supplied a concrete and material drafting template for the invitation to Sultan Mohamed V. C09 and C14 share the diplomatic salutation “Your Majesty” and general discussion of friendly bilateral relations, while C22 concerns welcoming a foreign leader during a visit to the United States. These similarities are conventional diplomatic-letter language or broad subject overlap. None reproduces the child’s distinctive progression from acknowledging the ruler’s letter, to discussing the Vice President’s report and bilateral negotiations, to extending a November invitation and arranging details through government representatives.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Your Majesty: I received with great pleasure your letter of March 8
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Your Majesty: It might be of interest to you to learn firsthand of General Collins' report to me
shared_material.explanation: C09 uses the same royal salutation and introduces an emissary’s report, but the wording, purpose, and ensuing structure differ materially.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the close ties which we have both worked to forge
shared_material.parent_excerpt: There is concrete evidence of the friendship that exists between our two countries
shared_material.explanation: C14 shares conventional bilateral-friendship language but contains no invitation machinery or parallel operative sequence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: to welcome you here in the United States
shared_material.parent_excerpt: let me assure you of a most sincere welcome on behalf of the people of the United States
shared_material.explanation: C22 has visit-and-welcome language, but it welcomes a leader whose trip is already occurring rather than extending an invitation and arranging a future visit.
